correctness.rationale: The idempotent correction w=sum D(e_v)e_v makes each derivation vertex-fixing modulo inner; in a loopless radical-square-zero quiver algebra the remaining derivations are arbitrary matrices on parallel arrow blocks, and inner gauges are exactly vertex-potential scalar differences. Composition powers in characteristic p yield block matrix powers. The Frobenius map is bijective on perfect fields, giving existence of a nilpotent block tuple; if two such tuples differ by a scalar gauge, the h-th power forces that gauge to vanish, proving uniqueness. Jordan orbit-centralizer formulas give exact counts; unique dominance-maximal bounded Jordan type gives an irreducible cone and the dimension formula. The finite quotient enumerator passed nine scenarios (including GF4 and a cycle-versus-tree test), direct Leibniz enumeration verified all 65536 binary maps on the 4D two-arrow Kronecker algebra and found 64 derivations/8 inner maps/8 classes/4 p-null classes, and seven matrix/Jordan formula comparisons passed. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove arbitrary dimensions.

originality.rationale: The closest primary sources determine Lie-algebra structure or general restricted invariance, not the finite-field count, all restricted heights and reduced geometry of the p-power-nilpotent outer-derivation cone. A restricted structure is extra information not determined by Lie brackets alone, and removing a vertex-scalar p-power coboundary by perfect-field roots is necessary for the new topology-independent bijection. Standard Jordan formulas alone count matrices, not outer-derivation classes. Actual semantic-record and literature searches found no equivalent or stronger direct statement. Uninspected broad literature may contain implicit coverage and absolute priority is not certified.

value.rationale: The restricted nilpotent cone and its higher p-power heights are natural invariants of modular Hochschild cohomology. The theorem gives a complete finite-field census and geometric irreducibility/dimension across arbitrary loopless multiquivers and unbounded parallel-arrow sizes, including graph cycles. It exhibits a meaningful structural distinction: cycles add ambient toral directions but leave all p-nilpotent height distributions unchanged. The cycle-versus-tree pair supplies an explicit motivated witness. The all-prime Frobenius normalization and exact Jordan partition product are not merely an arbitrary numerical slice or a trivial normalization check.
